segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Spieker Circle is the inscribed circle of the medial triangle M a M b M c. Named after nineteenth-century geometer Theodor Spieker, its center is the Spieker Center X ten, and its radius is r over two, half the inradius of triangle A B C.

subsegments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Spieker Circle is the inscribed circle of the medial triangle M a M b M c. Named after nineteenth-century geometer Theodor Spieker, its center is the Spieker Center X ten, and its radius is r over two, half the inradius of triangle A B C.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Because the medial triangle is the complement of triangle A B C under homothety at the Centroid X two, the Spieker circle is the exact complement of the incircle, and X ten lies on the Nagel line halfway between the Incenter X one and the Nagel Point X eight.

segments.text: Moreover, the Spieker Center X ten is the radical center of the three excircles of triangle A B C, and the Spieker circle is orthogonal to all three excircles in key radical projections.
